blocks.text: 1. Structured Output
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581612-554864822.png

Chain Of Thought's closing recap pointed forward to this topic. Structured Output, covering how prompting can shape the response into a defined format, moves from how the model reasons to how it presents the result.
It instructs the model to return its answer in a specific, predictable shape, a technique built on format rather than reasoning.
2. Why Downstream Code Needs Predictability
A free form paragraph answer cannot be reliably parsed by downstream code.
A structured response can be read the same way every single time.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Response style","Reliability for downstream code"],"rows":[["Free form paragraph","Cannot be reliably parsed every time"],["Structured response","Can be read the same way every time"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Defining The Expected Fields
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581612-657131916.png
Listing the exact fields the response should contain removes ambiguity about the output shape.
Each field name and its expected content is stated explicitly in the prompt.
4. Showing A Template Rather Than Describing It

blocks.alt: Showing A Template Rather Than Describing It
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581612-138896945.png
As with showing rather than telling the model, covered in Few-Shot Prompting, a literal template with placeholder text removes format ambiguity better than prose.
The model copies the visible structure rather than inferring it.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A literal template with bracketed placeholder text gives the model a concrete pattern to copy rather than leaving it to infer the intended structure from a written description alone.

blocks.text: 5. Delimiting Sections Clearly
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581612-952727731.png
Clear delimiters between sections help the model and downstream code both locate each part.
This reduces accidental blending between sections that belong apart.
6. Handling Fields With No Data
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581612-882818365.png
As with handling missing information explicitly, covered in System Prompting, a field with no available data needs an explicit placeholder rather than an omitted field.
This keeps the overall structure intact even when content is missing.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Field state","How to represent it"],"rows":[["Field has data","Fill in the field content directly"],["Field has no data","Use an explicit placeholder, never omit the field"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Models Still Deviate From The Format

blocks.alt: Models Still Deviate From The Format
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581817-52074684.png
Even a carefully specified structure can still be occasionally deviated from by the model.
Downstream code still needs to handle a malformed response gracefully.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Treating structured output prompting as a strong hint rather than a hard guarantee keeps downstream parsing code resilient to the occasional malformed response.

blocks.text: 8. Structured Output As A Step Before JSON
A labeled, delimited structure is a looser stepping stone toward the stricter JSON Output covered next.
It is easier for a model to follow reliably than strict machine syntax alone.
9. Recognizing When Structured Output Prompting Is Worth The Extra Instruction

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Structured Output Prompting Is Worth The Extra Instruction
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581818-746701278.png
Responses consumed by downstream code or a UI benefit most from a defined structure.
Casual, conversational answers often read better without rigid structure.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Describing the desired format in prose instead of showing a literal template.
Omitting a field entirely when there is no data, instead of using an explicit placeholder.
Assuming a specified structure will always be followed without validating the response.
Using rigid structured output for casual, conversational responses that do not need it.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Structured output prompting instructs the model to return its answer in a defined shape.
A free form paragraph answer cannot be reliably parsed by downstream code.
Listing the exact expected fields removes ambiguity about the output shape.
Showing a literal template with placeholders works better than describing the format in prose.
Clear delimiters between sections help both the model and downstream code locate each part.
Fields with no available data need an explicit placeholder rather than being omitted.
Even a well specified structure can still be occasionally deviated from by the model.
A labeled, delimited structure is a looser stepping stone toward stricter JSON output.
Next up: JSON Output, covering how prompting can produce strictly parseable machine format.
